incidents.name: Mini Shai-Hulud — TanStack worm
incidents.window_note: 84 malicious versions published across 42 @tanstack/* packages between 19:20 and 19:26 UTC via a compromised GitHub Actions release pipeline; approximate removal window per the TanStack postmortem. Campaign expanded to 172 packages and 403 versions across npm and PyPI within 48 hours.
incidents.payload: Harvests AWS/GCP/Kubernetes/Vault credentials, GitHub tokens and SSH keys; installs persistence in .claude/settings.json and .vscode/tasks.json that re-executes on every project open; a gh-token-monitor daemon polls GitHub every 60s and wipes the home directory if a stolen token is revoked; self-propagates by publishing to every npm package the stolen token can reach. First documented malicious npm packages shipping with valid SLSA provenance.
incidents.story: At 19:20 UTC the attacker turned TanStack's own release pipeline against it: 84 malicious artifacts across 42 packages in six minutes, each with valid provenance. @tanstack/react-router alone serves 12.7M downloads a week.
incidents.packages_note: Console loads the six highest-impact families; the advisory lists all 42 packages / 84 versions.

incidents.name: chalk / debug account takeover
incidents.window_note: A maintainer's npm account was phished via a fake 2FA-reset email from npmjs.help (registered three days earlier). Malicious versions of 18 foundational packages — 2.6 billion combined weekly downloads — were live for roughly two hours before the community caught them.
incidents.payload: Browser-side crypto-clipper: silently intercepts crypto and web3 activity, rewrites wallet interactions and payment destinations so funds and approvals are redirected to attacker-controlled accounts.
incidents.story: 13:16 UTC: eighteen packages that sit under practically every JavaScript build — chalk, debug, ansi-styles, strip-ansi — start shipping a crypto-clipper. They were downloaded 2.6 billion times a week.

incidents.name: Shai-Hulud worm — tinycolor wave
incidents.window_note: The first fully self-propagating npm worm: each infected package's postinstall stole npm tokens with TruffleHog and republished the payload to every package the token could reach. 500+ packages infected before containment; timestamps approximate.
incidents.payload: postinstall runs TruffleHog to harvest npm/GitHub/cloud credentials, exfiltrates them to a public GitHub repo named 'Shai-Hulud', then uses stolen npm tokens to trojanize and republish up to 20 more packages per victim — a worm, not a one-off.
incidents.story: The first true npm worm. Patient zero: @ctrl/tinycolor, 2.2M downloads a week. Every install became an infection vector, every stolen token a new publisher.
incidents.packages_note: Console loads the most-downloaded wave-1 packages; the full worm eventually touched 500+.
